scenarios: The plan's design assumes exclusive triggering and does not account for concurrent auto-compact / on-demand compaction interacting with the scheduled sweep (store-lock contention, HEAD drift on the tickets branch — see applier.py f058)

findings.finding: The plan asserts 'nothing else invokes compaction,' but multiple existing invocation paths do: on-demand `rebar compact <id>`, `rebar compact-all`, and the reconciler applier's auto-compact. This unverified capability/exclusivity claim is contradicted by prior art.
findings.location: Approach — 'The workflow is the trigger: nothing else invokes compaction.'

findings.finding: The workflow destructively rewrites/deletes source event files in the durable `tickets` store and must push the result, but the plan specifies no checkout depth, no concurrency guard, and no coordination with the reconcile-bridge workflow that also writes the same branch — a documented store-corruption / data-loss path.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — .github/workflows/compact-store.yml
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror reconcile-bridge.yml: checkout with fetch-depth: 0, add a concurrency group covering the tickets-branch writers, and push with --force-with-lease after a full-history merge.

findings.finding: The workflow must commit/push the compacted store back (compaction does git add -A + commit), but the plan does not state the checkout/write-credential/branch-push precondition the GitHub Action needs.
findings.location: Approach — 'checks out the tickets branch and runs rebar compact'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a reversibility/safety mechanism for the destructive compaction (e.g. write the compacted store to a temp path and atomically swap, retain a pre-compaction backup/snapshot, or document expand-contract), and add a test that compaction preserves replayable state.
evidence: 'The store's event log grows without bound, so a periodic compaction pass must run'
Testing lists only happy-path cron assertion and no-op-on-compact; no test for the destructive rewrite's safety.
findings.finding: Compaction rewrites/discards the event log — a destructive, irreversible operation — but the plan states no backup, rollback, or expand-contract safeguard; only a no-op-on-already-compact edge test is planned.
findings.location: Approach / Testing — 'runs `rebar compact`' and 'compaction on an already-compact store is a no-op'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a safeguard for the unattended log rewrite (backup/tag prior state, or fail-closed on integrity check) before the compacted result is persisted.
evidence: 'runs `rebar compact`' on a daily schedule with 'nothing else invokes compaction'
No safeguard, backup, or rollback mentioned for the log-rewrite operation
findings.finding: The plan does not consider blast radius/safeguard for the scheduled log rewrite: `rebar compact` rewrites the event log unattended daily with no stated backup, dry-run, or failure handling if compaction corrupts or truncates history.
findings.location: Approach / Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A buggy compaction pass silently drops events and the daily cron overwrites the good state before anyone notices

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the scheduled workflow handles writes that land on the tickets branch during compaction (fetch/rebase before push, fast-forward-only push, or lock coordination) so no concurrent write is clobbered or lost.
evidence: Approach says the workflow 'checks out the tickets branch and runs rebar compact' and stops there — no push-back / reconciliation step is specified
Compaction is a one-way transform: event_append.py notes 'replay/dedup/union-merge/compaction key off each event's UUID' and collapse is invisible only when complete
ABSENCE: neither Scope, Testing, nor Acceptance Criteria mentions concurrent writes during the scheduled run or how the compacted branch is pushed (ff vs force)
findings.finding: The plan schedules unattended compaction (a one-way rewrite of the persisted event log) but never specifies how the workflow reconciles writes that land on the tickets branch DURING the run, nor how it pushes the compacted result back (fast-forward vs force), so concurrent writes in the checkout->compact->push window can be clobbered or lost.
findings.location: Approach: 'checks out the tickets branch and runs rebar compact'
scenarios: A writer commits a new ticket event on the tickets branch while the daily workflow is running compaction on an older checkout; the workflow's push either force-overwrites the concurrent commit (lost write) or fails non-fast-forward and silently leaves the store un-compacted

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify failure handling for the compaction job: atomic/idempotent write so a mid-run crash leaves the store intact, and surface job failure (non-zero exit + workflow failure notification) rather than swallowing it.
evidence: 'a periodic compaction pass must run on its own'
No mention of failure handling, atomic write, or alerting on job failure.
findings.finding: The scheduled workflow performs a write/rewrite of the store with no error handling, no idempotency guarantee beyond no-op-on-compact, no crash-safety for partial compaction, and no observability/alert when the cron job fails.
findings.location: Approach — 'a GitHub Actions workflow on a daily `schedule:` cron ... runs `rebar compact`'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define concurrency handling for compaction against the shared store/branch (e.g. a workflow concurrency group / lock, or atomic read-modify-write) so a concurrent store write cannot be lost.
evidence: 'checks out the tickets branch and runs `rebar compact`'
Compaction reads-then-rewrites the event log; concurrent writes to the same branch are unaddressed.
findings.finding: The store's event log is shared state mutated by compaction, but the plan does not address concurrency: a normal store write (or another workflow committing to the tickets branch) racing with compaction could cause a lost update or TOCTOU on the shared branch.
findings.location: Approach — 'checks out the tickets branch and runs `rebar compact`'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a compaction failure/edge test (e.g., interrupted or partial compaction, malformed event) asserting the store is left intact rather than corrupted.
evidence: Testing lists only: 'Happy path: ... cron is daily and its job runs rebar compact' and 'Edge: ... already-compact store is a no-op'
Compaction rewrites/truncates an append-only event log — a data-mutating operation with real failure modes not covered
findings.finding: The compaction entry point (compact.py) is new behavior that transforms the event log, but testing only covers happy-path and an already-compact no-op; failure/edge paths (interrupted/partial compaction, malformed or unreadable events, concurrent writes during a scheduled run) are not addressed.
findings.location: Testing section
scenarios: A scheduled compaction is interrupted mid-write and leaves the store in an inconsistent state
The log contains a malformed/unreadable event and compaction must fail safely rather than corrupt the store

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure-notification/alerting mechanism (or explicitly justify relying on run history) so a silently-failing scheduled compaction is surfaced.
evidence: 'Compaction runs unattended once a day, verified by the workflow's run history.'
No mention of failure notification/alerting for a silently-failing scheduled job
findings.finding: No observability/failure ownership is specified for the new scheduled workflow; the AC relies on 'the workflow's run history' as the only verification, with no alerting when a scheduled compaction fails.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'verified by the workflow's run history'
scenarios: Scheduled compaction starts failing and, since no one watches run history, the log resumes unbounded growth undetected

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and test the partial-failure/interruption behavior of the scheduled run — that compaction is atomic or resumable/idempotent and leaves the store consistent (with a back-out path) when a run is cancelled or fails mid-way.
evidence: Testing lists only 'schedule cron is daily', 'job runs rebar compact', and 'compaction on an already-compact store is a no-op'
AC2 relies on 'the workflow's run history' as verification but does not require the run to leave the store consistent on failure
ABSENCE: no statement on partial-failure/rollback or resumability of an interrupted scheduled compaction
findings.finding: The plan gives compaction a new unattended operating mode but does not assert what happens on partial failure or interruption of a scheduled run (crash mid-compaction, push failure), nor that a re-run is idempotent/resumable and leaves the store consistent — the only failure-adjacent test is 'no-op on an already-compact store'.
findings.location: Testing / Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: The daily workflow is cancelled or the runner dies mid-compaction; the next day's run must re-run cleanly without double-applying or leaving orphaned/partial state, but the plan never asserts this

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Expose compaction as a shape-agnostic entry point (the `rebar compact` CLI/library call is invocable directly) and treat the GitHub Actions workflow as ONE optional scheduling venue, so non-GitHub consumers can also trigger compaction.
evidence: 'The workflow is the trigger: nothing else invokes compaction.'
rebar must run as a Python library, CLI, and remote MCP server against many target projects; a GitHub Actions cron is only available for repos hosted on GitHub with Actions enabled.
findings.finding: The plan makes a GitHub Actions scheduled workflow the SOLE trigger for compaction ('nothing else invokes compaction'), so rebar consumers not running on GitHub-hosted Actions get no compaction and an unbounded store.
findings.location: Approach — 'The workflow is the trigger: nothing else invokes compaction.'
scenarios: Remote MCP server / server outside the checkout: rebar drives a target project whose git remote is self-hosted (GitLab/Gitea) or has GitHub Actions disabled — the daily cron never fires, so `rebar compact` is never invoked and the event log grows without bound (the exact problem the plan sets out to solve remains unfixed for that consumer).
Target project on a developer workstation with no CI: the store still grows unbounded because the only compaction path is a GitHub-hosted schedule.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-line positive rationale for the daily GitHub Actions cron approach (why it fits: unattended, repo-native scheduling, no store-lock contention when run in a clone), so the choice is defensible against the existing out-of-band-sweep design.
evidence: Approach states the mechanism ('a GitHub Actions workflow on a daily schedule: cron ... The workflow is the trigger') but gives no 'why this fits' rationale
An alternative — the documented out-of-band dedicated-clone sweep (transition_close.py:489-491) — already exists as a design and is not weighed
findings.finding: The plan states no positive rationale for choosing a GitHub Actions daily-cron workflow (over, e.g., reusing the existing compact-on-write hooks, or an out-of-band sweep already scaffolded in the codebase). Absent rationale, the approach cannot be judged fit against alternatives.
findings.location: Approach section
scenarios: Reviewers/implementers cannot tell whether the daily-cron GH Actions design was chosen deliberately over the existing sweep design.
